skill.description: Raw mechanical interfaces fusing Swiss typographic print with military terminal aesthetics. Rigid grids, extreme type scale contrast, utilitarian color, analog degradation effects. skill.summary: Create strict industrial brutalist interfaces with dense grids, oversized typography, utilitarian palettes, and tactical telemetry details.

content.value_statement: Many data-heavy interfaces look generic and visually soft. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code precise industrial brutalist UI rules for grids, type, color, and texture.
actual_capabilities: Guides Swiss industrial print and tactical telemetry interface styles.
Defines typography rules for macro headers, micro data, and limited serif contrast.
Specifies strict light and dark color palettes with one red accent.
Directs rigid grid layouts, visible dividers, sharp corners, and dense information zones.
Recommends analog effects such as halftones, dithering, scanlines, and mechanical noise.
limitations: It provides design direction, not complete application code.
It focuses on one visual style and may not suit consumer or playful products.
It does not include accessibility testing or performance validation.
It does not provide reusable assets, templates, or component libraries.

use_cases.title: Design Dense Dashboards
use_cases.description: Create dashboard layouts that use rigid grids, compact metadata, and high contrast information zones.

use_cases.title: Build Editorial Interfaces
use_cases.description: Apply oversized typography, strict spacing, and industrial print rules to portfolio or editorial pages.

use_cases.title: Define Visual Direction
use_cases.description: Turn a vague brutalist brief into a clear palette, type system, layout model, and texture plan.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Style Direction
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new interface concept.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the industrial-brutalist-ui skill to define a visual direction for a data dashboard. Include palette, typography, layout, and texture guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign A Screen
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for improving an existing page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the industrial-brutalist-ui skill to redesign this screen. Preserve the content hierarchy and make the interface feel mechanical and data dense.

prompt_templates.title: Specify Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to specify navigation, tables, status indicators, buttons, and telemetry panels for a tactical dashboard.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Visual System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for critique and refinement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this interface against the industrial-brutalist-ui skill. Identify style conflicts, weak hierarchy, palette drift, and missing brutalist details.

output_examples.input: A fintech dashboard needs a harder visual system.
output_examples.output: The result uses a light Swiss industrial palette, black structural dividers, oversized account numerals, and red only for urgent deltas.

output_examples.input: A monitoring console should feel like tactical telemetry.
output_examples.output: The result uses a dark CRT substrate, monospaced metadata, compact status rows, scanline texture, and one controlled green status readout.

output_examples.input: A portfolio page needs brutalist editorial structure.
output_examples.output: The result uses massive uppercase headings, asymmetric whitespace, rigid compartments, sparse serif contrast, and visible mechanical registration marks.

best_practices: Choose either Swiss industrial print or tactical telemetry before designing.
Use red as a controlled accent for alerts, dividers, or vital data only.
Pair dense technical zones with large structural typography for contrast.
anti_patterns: Do not mix light and dark substrates within the same interface.
Do not use gradients, soft shadows, rounded corners, or casual consumer patterns.
Do not let decorative technical details reduce readability or hierarchy.

faq.question: What kind of projects fit this skill?
faq.answer: It fits dashboards, editorial systems, portfolios, and technical interfaces that need a severe industrial visual language.

faq.question: Does this skill generate production code?
faq.answer: No. It provides design rules and implementation direction that can guide generated code.

faq.question: Can I use it for mobile interfaces?
faq.answer: Yes, but dense telemetry layouts need careful responsive planning and accessibility review.

faq.question: Does it require a dark terminal theme?
faq.answer: No. It supports either a light Swiss industrial print mode or a dark tactical telemetry mode.

faq.question: What should the main accent color be?
faq.answer: Use aviation red as the primary accent. Terminal green should appear only for one purposeful status element.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to install?
faq.answer: The reviewed file is documentation only. Static alerts came from markdown examples, not executable behavior.
